extracted.intended_audience: prospective creative-writing students (adult writers) seeking short, single-session classes or workshops
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of GrubStreet's single-session short classes and weekend workshops: what to expect, formats, pedagogical approaches, and entrypoints for new students. Focused on short (3- or 6-hour) sessions in-person or online that concentrate on particular craft topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-session length (3 or 6 hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: These short classes meet one time for three or six hours, usually on Fridays and Saturdays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-hour seminars provide a concentrated session; six-hour weekend workshops give a whole day for deeper work. Expect scheduling on weekends and single-meeting commitment rather than multi-week courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery mode and location
rubrics_metrics.description: Classes are offered either in-person at the Center for Creative Writing in Boston, or on Zoom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose between attending on-site or remotely; logistics and experience may differ by mode. Sessions are commonly scheduled on Fridays and Saturdays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focused topical scope / deep dive
rubrics_metrics.description: Short classes are a fantastic way to do a deep dive into a particular subject–like writing about fruit, overcoming writer's block, tackling the MFA application, ekphrastic poetry, or perfecting that first sentence of your novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect tightly focused content on a single topic or technique. Examples indicate both quirky micro-topics and core craft concerns; classes hone in on one subject rather than broad surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-hour seminars hone in on a single aspect
rubrics_metrics.description: These three-hour sessions hone in on a single aspect of the writing process or the writing life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seminars function as crash courses or focused skill sessions (e.g., how to pitch an agent, mastering omniscient POV, dialogue mechanics, or exploring a new essay form). They are suited for targeted skill development rather than long-form practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-hour weekend workshops for broader craft work
rubrics_metrics.description: In a weekend workshop, writers have a whole day to dig into a broader element of craft, through generative exercises and on-the-spot feedback sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshops emphasize generative practice and immediate feedback, and may address broader processes like revision, point of view, or introductions to new genres. Use workshops for hands-on development and revision-oriented learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active participation and peer connection expected
rubrics_metrics.description: In any of our short classes, you can expect to participate in writing exercises and connect with other writers who share your interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are participatory, practice-based sessions — passive listening is not the norm. Expect exercises, possibly sharing work, and opportunities to network with fellow writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free sessions and Open House as entrypoints and advising
rubrics_metrics.description: New to Grub and not sure where to start? Check out our free sessions! A few times a month, both in-person and on Zoom, we hold free writing sessions to whet your creative whistle and connect with other writers. Once a term several staff members come together to host Open House events, where students can find out about new classes and get advice on the courses that best suit their needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use free sessions and Open Houses to sample offerings, get orientation, and receive staff recommendations. These are low-commitment ways to determine fit before registering for paid classes.
